support_spans: Histopathology of finger tumor
brown coloration of osteolytic cysts
Numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei
candidates.why: The presence of a tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger with histopathological features of fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells with multiple osteoclast-like nuclei is consistent with a brown tumor.

candidates.name: Hyperparathyroidism-related Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica
support_spans: primary hyperparathyroidism
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Hypophosphatemia at 0.65 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
candidates.why: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels are consistent with osteitis fibrosa cystica.

giant multinucleated cells dispersed in contact with fibers
candidates.why: The presence of giant cells with multiple osteoclast-like nuclei and giant multinucleated cells is consistent with a giant cell tumor.

key_evidence_spans: Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei

candidates.name: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
support_spans: Histopathology of finger tumor
Numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei and giant multinucleated cells dispersed in contact with fibers associated with small vessels
candidates.why: The presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger with histopathological features of fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells is consistent with a brown tumor, a known complication of hyperparathyroidism.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and the fact that it can be mistaken for other bone lesions.

candidates.name: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
support_spans: Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption in the phalangeal tuft band
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance
candidates.why: The radiographic findings of bone resorption and the 'salt-and-pepper' appearance of the skull are characteristic of osteitis fibrosa cystica, a condition often associated with hyperparathyroidism.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis requires careful consideration of the patient's hyperparathyroidism history and the specific radiographic features.

candidates.name: Parathyroid carcinoma
support_spans: Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Sestamibi parathyroid scintigraphy identified hyperfunctional nodule
candidates.why: The extremely high level of parathyroid hormone and the presence of a hyperfunctional nodule on scintigraphy raise the possibility of parathyroid carcinoma, a rare but aggressive form of hyperparathyroidism.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis is important to consider due to its potential for aggressive behavior and the need for prompt surgical intervention.

key_evidence_spans: Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption in the phalangeal tuft band

selector.rationale: The histopathology of the finger tumor showing brown coloration of osteolytic cysts and numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei is most consistent with Brown Tumor, which is a known complication of primary hyperparathyroidism.

rejected.label: Parathyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: While elevated serum parathyroid hormone and a hyperfunctional nodule on sestamibi parathyroid scintigraphy are concerning for parathyroid carcinoma, the presence of a brown tumor and the patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Tumor
rejected.why: Although the histopathology shows giant cells, the clinical and radiographic context, including the patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism and the presence of a brown tumor, make Giant Cell Tumor a less likely diagnosis.
